**Pre-release for testing — not a stable version.** Clean-room Rust post-processor for scanned books: split → deskew → crop → clean/binarize → PDF with an OCR text layer. GUI in 8 languages (ro, en, fr, it, es, pt, de, hu) and command line. MIT licence, runs locally, no accounts.

## Downloads
Pick the archive for your system; every archive has a `.sha256` next to it.

| System | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Linux x86-64 / ARM64 | `*-linux-gnu.tar.gz` | glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 and later); OpenGL 2+, X11 or Wayland |
| Windows x86-64 | `*-windows-msvc.zip` | no Visual C++ Redistributable needed; OpenGL 2+ |
| macOS Apple-silicon / Intel | `*-apple-darwin.zip` | unsigned: right-click → Open on first launch |

OCR works out of the box with the built-in engine; Tesseract is used instead when it is installed with the languages you ask for (`--engine auto`, the default).

## New since 0.2.0-pre.4
- **Built-in OCR engine (pure Rust, nothing to install).** Reads ro, en, fr, it, es, pt, de, hu: page layout analysis, a small neural line recogniser written from scratch (own inference code, no external library), dictionary-assisted error repair, automatic levelling of crooked pages, light-on-dark pages, ruled tables, long lines, and 0/90/180/270° orientation detection that also serves `--auto-rotate` without Tesseract. `--engine auto|native|tesseract`.
- **Honest limits of that engine:** the model was trained only on synthetic text rendered from open fonts. On clean synthetic pages it makes about 0.6 % character errors (`docs/OCR-BENCH.md`); it has **not** been measured on real scans, where Tesseract may well be better. `auto` therefore prefers an installed Tesseract that has the requested languages. Its word lists are CC BY-SA 4.0 data (`LEXICONS-NOTICE.md`); build with `--no-default-features` to leave them out.
- **Security and robustness (whole-project adversarial review, ~60 findings).** PDF: crash/out-of-memory on hostile predictor and CCITT parameters, decoded-bytes and visit budgets, JBIG2 and JPEG 2000 bombs, fake objects hidden in stream data, object-stream revisions, encrypted palettes, V4 key length; scans placed mirrored or turned are shown as the PDF displays them. CLI: page images can no longer overwrite the input scans, a failed image save no longer loses the PDF/text, numeric options are validated. Engine: archive bombs are stopped while extracting, unreadable zip members are reported, search finds hyphenated words and decomposed accents, project files cannot be tricked with odd file names, GUI project files cannot choose the OCR program. CI: release tag no longer reaches the shell unchecked, actions pinned to commits, read-only default permissions.
- **Picture detector:** the paper level is judged per tile, so text on a lighting gradient is no longer taken for a picture (from `main`, after pre.4).
- **Pipeline:** blank sheets keep the requested page size, `--max-skew` is a hard limit, crooked spreads find their gutter, bilevel downscaling keeps thin rules, bounded memory for blur on huge scans.

- **From the "Workshop" recommendations:** `--json` (structured OCR output with word boxes); `--search-preset` (Romanian CUI, IBAN, invoice, e-mail, phone, date, amount) and `--search-help`; wildcards `?` / `*` and `A NEAR/n B` proximity in `--search`.

## Known limits
- The native OCR engine has only been validated on synthetic pages (see above); no real-scan accuracy claim is made.
- PDF/A-2b is checked with veraPDF on generated samples only; it is not a certification of every output.
- JBIG2 Huffman coding and some JPEG 2000 code-block styles are decoded only through an installed `pdftoppm`, `mutool` or Ghostscript.
- Only the empty user password is tried on encrypted PDFs. Very faint pencil pages can count as blank.
- 7z and rar archives were NOT tested (no extractor was available to the author). Verified by hand on Linux x86-64 only; the Windows, macOS and ARM64 builds come from CI. The GUI was smoke-tested, not exercised in depth.

Documentation and presentation: https://legatorocr.chiuta.ro · Source and comparison with other tools: README.md, COMPARISON.md.
